title: Tucker Carlson Launches New Show Claiming Atlantis Was Home to Bible Giants

content:
​Tucker Carlson recently launched a new History channel-style docuseries that claims to put conspiracy theories to the test. Shadow Figures is hosted by former Marine and defense contractor Chad Robichaux, a Christian conservative who leads a team of ex-military members as they investigate conspiracies and pseudoscience. While most of the investigations in the members-only series are beyond my scope, the third episode is set to explore whether Atlantis is real. Robichaux previewed it while joining Carlson a few days ago to promote the new show.

​Robichaux told Carlson that he approached the question of Atlantis from a Christian perspective, identifying Plato’s ancient empire with the antediluvian world described in the Book of Genesis. (Ignatius Donnelly had already done the same, as had Cosmas Indicopleustes back in the sixth century.) He asserts that the Flood was a real event and that Atlantis was located in the Bermuda Triangle along the so-called Bimini Road, a natural formation that he falsely asserts was a major thoroughfare leading to Atlantis. (To judge by his interview’s many topics, all his conspiracy theories come from the 1970s.)

 However, Robichaux has closely aligned his views with one of his and Carlson’s “favorite” people, Christian Nephilim-hunter Timothy Alberino (from whom he adopted the Bimini-as-Atlantis claim, calling his version “beautiful” and “perfect”), and therefore uses the Book of Enoch and the myth of the Watchers to explain the story of Atlantis, but with a defiantly non-canonical twist, arguing that Satan used the Watchers to “infect that bloodline” of humanity in a “seed war,” so humans begged God to save them from the giants, leading God to send the flood to preserve the purest blood. This is a radical departure from mainstream Christianity—and, for that matter, the literal words of Genesis 6:5-7, where God explicitly identified humans, not giant hybrids, as the wickedness that caused him to regret his creation—but it is in keeping with the eugenics of modern conservatives.

 And where there is eugenics, racism isn’t far behind. During the conversation, which involved a discussion of megalithic architecture and even North American mounds, the two men descended into the kind of rank racism even Ancient Aliens has tried to soften over the years. Robichaux described Machu Picchu as being thousands of years older than conventional archaeology dates it, and he and Carlson agreed that “some primitive little mountain tribal person didn’t build this.”

 Robichaux and Carlson also spent time complaining that archaeologists and historians aren’t investigating Atlantis, the lost race of Bible giants, and the Watchers’ secret technology. Robichaux falsely asserts that the Smithsonian has suppressed all of the evidence for Bible giants—a malicious claim I have explored many times on this blog, but which traces back to David Childress’s 1990s-era conspiracy theory about the Smithsonian destroying evidence of a lost civilization, mitigated through Ross Hamilton’s efforts to apply that to giants. As I explained many times in the past, when bones alleged to be those of giants were sent to the Smithsonian, they were correctly identified as either megafauna bones and sent to the paleontology section of the natural history collection or correctly identified as mismeasured human bones and, well, sent to the human branch of the natural history collection.

 The two men discuss the hoax of the so-called “Kandahar Giant,” which I have covered many times before, and most of the discussion in this lengthy segment boils down to an argument that the Bible is literally true and therefore archaeologists must be conspiring to hide evidence of Noah’s Flood and the Genesis 6 giants.

 And, really, I have to give Tucker Carlson and Chad Robichaux a little bit of credit for correctly identifying the subtext of the kind of History channel shows popular more than a decade ago—Biblical inerrancy, white nationalism, and rage at elites—and foregrounding it more explicitly than the History channel ever dared to back when it was busy paving the way for Trumpism.
